Map atlas

Synthetic sample site, Chester County PA

4 parcels, 15.09 acres with all parcels merged. Prepared November 14, 2026 from county parcel lines and public geospatial services. Each page shows one map, what the layer is and where it comes from, and what it shows on this site. Thresholds used: slope limit 15%, property-line setback 50 ft, stream buffer 100 ft, wetland buffer 50 ft. These are working assumptions until checked against the municipal ordinance.

Base map

Parcels

County parcel polygons for the listing (yellow dashed lines) over current aerial imagery, with the dissolved outer boundary in red. Areas are computed from the geometry in EPSG:2272 after reprojection from the county's export, so they are the mapped acreage, which can differ from deed acreage. The recorded (deed) acreage totals 15.20 acres. Parcel lines from county GIS are compiled from deeds and tax maps and are not a survey; expect differences of a few feet along boundaries.

Terrain

Slope

Percent slope derived from the USGS 3DEP digital elevation model at 10 ft resolution, with 10 ft contours. Green is gentle, red is steep. Slope matters for three reasons: most municipalities restrict building on slopes above 15% or 25%, driveways and septic fields need gentle ground, and steep ground erodes when disturbed. On this site 0.7 acres (4%) are steeper than 15%.

Buildable area

Yellow is ground that passes every test: slope at or below 15%, more than 50 ft from the outer property line, outside mapped flood zones, and more than 100 ft from streams and 50 ft from wetlands. Shaded areas show which constraint removes each part. Black outlines are contiguous buildable patches of at least 0.5 acres, the candidate building pads.

2.48 acres (16.4%) are buildable. Removed by: steep 0.68 ac, setback 3.85 ac, flood 11.99 ac, stream buffer 2.89 ac, wetland buffer 3.86 ac, drainage way buffer 1.97 ac. Accepting slopes up to 25% would give 2.48 acres.

The setback is applied uniformly to the outer boundary, not per zoning yard rules, and the slope limit is a placeholder. Both are set in the listing file and should be matched to the ordinance.

Evaluation

Winter sun

Left: hours of direct sun on December 21, the shortest day, found by casting shadows across the elevation model every half hour from sunrise to sunset at latitude 40.1711. Right: a winter solar index that also accounts for the angle at which sunlight strikes the slope, relative to flat open ground (1.0). A south-facing slope scores above 1, a north-facing slope below, because low winter sun hits it obliquely.

Flat open ground here gets 8.8 hours. The property averages 8.6 h (index 0.98); the buildable area averages 8.7 h (index 1.0). 70.9% of the ground faces south-east to south-west or is flat.

The elevation model is bare earth. Tree canopy and neighbouring buildings are not included, so on a wooded site real sun at ground level is lower than shown until clearing.

Evaluation

Stormwater

Blue lines show where water concentrates as it flows downhill, from filling depressions in the elevation model and routing each cell to its steepest neighbour. Darker blue carries more upslope area. Orange dots mark where concentrated flow leaves the property, labelled with the acres draining to that point. Magenta marks depressions that would pond more than half a foot deep. Cyan lines are mapped streams, green is mapped wetland.

23.56 acres of neighbouring land drain onto the property. About 1870 ft of concentrated flow paths (at least 1.0 acre contributing) cross it, and 0.253 acres would pond.

Evaluation

Growing ground

Ground classed for cultivation rather than construction, so no property-line setback is applied. Green is garden-grade: slope at or below 8%, at least 8 hours of direct sun on June 21, and soil that is not poorly drained, hydric or mapped wetland. Light green suits orchards and terraced beds (slope to 20%); fruit trees tolerate slopes well and benefit from the cold-air drainage a hillside gives. Straw is pasture or meadow (slope to 25%). Blue is wet ground, better for a wet meadow or pond than vegetables. Brown is steep or shaded ground best left as woodlot.

11.06 acres are garden-grade, 1.46 acres orchard or terrace, 0.15 acres pasture. 10.05 acres of garden and orchard ground lie outside the buildable area. Counting building, growing and grazing together, 12.67 acres (84.0%) of the property are usable. USDA rates 0.00 acres as prime farmland soil and 0.00 acres as farmland of statewide importance.

Evaluation

Restrictions and context

Designations, easements, utilities, traffic and taxes that restrict what can be done or cost money, and are easy to miss in a listing. Deed restrictions, rights of way and pending zoning changes still need a title search and a call to the municipality.

    Sources: National Park Service, WeConservePA, county GIS, PennDOT, PA DEP, USDA Soil Data Access, county assessment export.

    FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, flood hazard zones

    FEMA flood hazard zones. Zone A and AE are the 1% annual-chance (100-year) floodplain, where building is restricted and flood insurance is required with a mortgage. Zone X is outside the mapped floodplain.

    Covers 15.09 acres (100.0% of the property).

    FLD_ZONEacrespct_of_property
    A11.99879.5
    X3.08920.5
    What the codes mean. FEMA flood zones. "Special Flood Hazard Area" (SFHA) zones have a 1% chance of flooding in any year (the "100-year" flood); building there needs a floodplain permit and flood insurance with a mortgage.
    • A: SFHA, 1% annual-chance floodplain, no base flood elevation determined.
    • X: Outside the 1% annual-chance floodplain. Minimal flood hazard (unshaded X) or, where the subtype says 0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE, the moderate 500-year floodplain (shaded X).
    https://hazards.fema.gov/arcgis/rest/services/public/NFHL/MapServer/28, fetched 2026-11-13

    USGS National Hydrography Dataset, streams (large scale)

    Census TIGER local roads

    Street centerlines with ownership. Frontage on a state road can mean a PennDOT highway occupancy permit for a new driveway; municipal roads are handled by the township.

    Centerlines run along the road, not inside the parcel; frontage is the boundary length within 40 ft of a centerline: Coventryville Rd 404 ft.

    https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/Transportation/MapServer/8, fetched 2026-11-13. Source: U.S. Census Bureau
    Appendix

    Data sources

    Remote layers were fetched for the parcels' extent plus a margin and cached in the repository, so the maps can be regenerated and will not change until the cache is refreshed. Parcel lines and assessment attributes are the county's export. The elevation model is bare earth lidar from USGS 3DEP.
